quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: This is a start-of-word contrast. Listen for the puff of air as the lips open.
quests.explanation: It was "pace": the lips released with a clear puff before the vowel began. "Base" would slip into the vowel with the voice already running.
quests.vowelTensionRule: At the start of a word, /p/ is released with a small puff of air (aspiration) and no vocal-fold vibration; /b/ has little or no puff and voicing starts almost immediately.
quests.mouthPosition: Close both lips. For /p/ release them with a clear burst of air; for /b/ release them gently and start the vowel immediately.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: The change is in the middle of the word, between the vowels. Listen for a buzz.
quests.explanation: "Racing" has a clean hiss between the two vowels. "Raising" keeps the voice on through the middle and buzzes.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Between vowels, /s/ is a clean hiss and /z/ keeps the voice buzzing; the preceding vowel is a little longer before /z/.
quests.mouthPosition: Keep the tongue tip near the ridge behind your teeth. For /z/ vibrate the vocal folds; for /s/ let out only air.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Now the change is at the end. How long is the vowel, and how does it finish?
quests.explanation: What you caught was "prove": the vowel ran a little longer and the word finished on a soft buzz. "Proof" would end on a breathy hiss.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Vowel length is the most dependable cue here.
quests.mouthPosition: Stretch the vowel before /v/; shorten it before /f/.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Start-of-word again. Does the tongue tip release with a breath or without?
quests.explanation: "Dent" starts with the voice nearly immediate and no puff. "Tent" starts with a sharp, breathy release.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Initial /t/ is released with a puff of air and no voicing; initial /d/ has little puff and voicing begins almost at once. Aspiration is the audible clue.
quests.mouthPosition: Touch the tongue tip to the ridge behind your upper teeth, then release. Add a puff of air for /t/; let the voice start straight away for /d/.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: The clue is at the end. Listen to the vowel before the final stop.
quests.explanation: That was "league": the long vowel stretched a little more and the tongue closed softly. "Leak" is crisper and ends with a firmer click.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Word-final /ɡ/ is often partly devoiced in British English, so don't wait for the buzz; measure the vowel.
quests.mouthPosition: The back of the tongue rises to the soft palate in both; only the timing differs.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Middle-of-the-word contrast. Listen to the lips between the vowel and the /l/.
quests.explanation: "Staple" closes the lips with a tight, breathy pop. "Stable" keeps the voice buzzing across the lip closure.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Between vowels /p/ is crisp and voiceless while /b/ keeps the voice on through a softer closure. Listen for a sharper release and a shorter, brighter vowel before /p/.
quests.mouthPosition: Close the lips firmly and release with a crisp burst for /p/. For /b/ keep the throat buzzing while the lips close.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Same sound, now in the middle. Listen to the length of the first vowel.
quests.explanation: You heard "rider": the vowel was a little longer and the tongue tap was voiced. "Writer" has a shorter vowel and a crisper tongue-tip stop.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Between vowels, /t/ is a crisp voiceless stop while /d/ remains voiced and slightly softer; the vowel before /d/ is also a little longer. (Here we are using careful British pronunciation, not the American 'flap'.)
quests.mouthPosition: Tap the tongue tip on the ridge behind the teeth. For /t/ make it crisp with a brief silence; for /d/ keep the voice buzzing.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Back to the beginning of the word. Hiss or buzz?
quests.explanation: "Zinc" opens with a buzzing /z/ you can feel in your throat. "Sink" opens with a silent hiss.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /z/ carries vibration from the vocal folds; /s/ does not.
quests.mouthPosition: Keep the teeth close and the air stream narrow for both sounds.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Word-final now. Listen for the vowel length before the lips close.
quests.explanation: "Rib" gives the vowel a little more time and closes the lips softly. "Rip" is snappier and ends with a crisp pop.
quests.vowelTensionRule: At the end of a word, the vowel before /b/ is longer than before /p/, and /p/ ends with a crisp stop while /b/ ends softly and may be only partly voiced. Vowel length is the most reliable cue.
quests.mouthPosition: For /p/ close the lips quickly and stop the air. For /b/ hold the vowel longer, then close the lips softly.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Beginning of the word. Is there a breathy release at the back of the tongue?
quests.explanation: It was "gave": a soft, voiced start. "Cave" opens with a puff of air.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Initial /k/ has a strong puff of air and is voiceless; /ɡ/ has very little puff and voicing starts quickly. Both are made at the back of the tongue.
quests.mouthPosition: Raise the back of the tongue to the soft palate. Release with a puff of air for /k/; with a soft, voiced release for /ɡ/.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Listen to the middle of the word, between the two vowels.
quests.explanation: "Saver" has a soft, buzzing friction between the vowels. "Safer" has a clear breathy hiss.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Between vowels, /f/ is a clear hiss and /v/ keeps the voice on through a softer, buzzier friction.
quests.mouthPosition: Lightly touch the lower lip to the upper teeth. For /v/ let the throat buzz; for /f/ blow air with no vibration.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: End of the word. Which vowel is longer, and how does the closure feel?
quests.explanation: What you caught was "bid": a slightly longer vowel and a soft tongue-tip closure. "Bit" cuts the vowel short and closes sharply.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Ignore the final release; listen to how long the vowel is.
quests.mouthPosition: Keep the throat relaxed for /d/; tighten and stop for /t/.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: The first sound decides it. Listen for a buzz at the very start.
quests.explanation: "Fault" starts with a hiss, and the throat stays quiet. "Vault" starts with a buzz.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Voicing is the only difference, so tune into the vibration.
quests.mouthPosition: Keep the lip contact light and let the air escape through the gap.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Middle contrast. Listen for a tight closure or a soft, buzzing one between the vowels.
quests.explanation: That was "tapping": the lips shut tightly and released with a breathy pop. "Tabbing" would stay voiced right through the middle.
quests.vowelTensionRule: In the middle of a word, the voiceless /p/ has a tight closure and a small burst; /b/ is looser and slightly buzzy.
quests.mouthPosition: Touch your throat: for /b/ you feel vibration during the lip closure, for /p/ you do not.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Word-final friction. Long vowel plus buzz, or shorter vowel plus hiss?
quests.explanation: "Lose" lets the vowel run and ends with a buzz. "Loose" is shorter and ends on a hiss.
quests.vowelTensionRule: A longer vowel signals /z/; a shorter vowel and a strong hiss signal /s/.
quests.mouthPosition: Feel your throat vibrate through the end of /z/.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: In the middle of the word, listen for how the consonant sounds between the vowels.
quests.explanation: "Bicker" has a crisp, breathy /k/ between the vowels. "Bigger" is voiced throughout and sounds smoother.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Between vowels, /k/ is voiceless with a crisp release, while /ɡ/ stays voiced and softer, and the vowel before /ɡ/ is slightly longer.
quests.mouthPosition: Press the back of the tongue against the soft palate. For /k/ release with a crisp burst; for /ɡ/ keep the voice buzzing.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Start-of-word. Puff or no puff?
quests.explanation: The word was "bill": the lips opened softly and the voice was ready at once. "Pill" would start with a burst of breath.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Both are lip stops. The cue is the puff: strong for /p/, weak for /b/. Hold a hand or a tissue in front of your mouth and feel the difference.
quests.mouthPosition: Hold a tissue in front of your lips: it should flutter for /p/ but hardly move for /b/.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: End of the word. Listen to how long the vowel lasts.
quests.explanation: "Herd" holds the vowel a little longer, then closes softly. "Hurt" is shorter and finishes with a tongue-tip stop.
quests.vowelTensionRule: At the end of a word, the vowel or sonorant before /d/ lasts longer than before /t/. /t/ is short and sharp; /d/ is longer, softer and partly voiced.
quests.mouthPosition: Touch the tongue tip to the ridge behind the teeth. For /t/ shorten the vowel and stop at once; for /d/ hold the vowel longer and close softly.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Word-final. Listen for the last bit of friction.
quests.explanation: You heard "save": the vowel lingered and the word ended on a gentle buzz. "Safe" would end on a breathy hiss.
quests.vowelTensionRule: At the end of a word, the voiced /v/ lengthens the vowel before it and often ends weakly; /f/ shortens the vowel and finishes with a strong hiss.
quests.mouthPosition: Touch the lower lip to the upper teeth. For /f/ end with clear breathy friction; for /v/ keep the voice buzzing and hold the vowel a little longer.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Initial position. Listen for the puff before the /j/ sound.
quests.explanation: "Tune" starts with a breathy release that carries over into the glide. "Dune" starts with the voice on right away.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Both stops are made with the tongue tip on the ridge behind the upper teeth. /t/ adds a burst of breath, /d/ does not.
quests.mouthPosition: A tissue held in front of your mouth should move for /t/ but hardly for /d/.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: The consonant sits between vowels. Hiss or buzz?
quests.explanation: What you caught was "lazy": the middle consonant buzzed with the voice running. "Lacy" has a clean hiss in the middle.
quests.vowelTensionRule: The buzz of /z/ continues through the consonant; /s/ interrupts the voice.
quests.mouthPosition: Feel the throat vibrate for /z/.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: The last sound is where the words split. Which ending is softer?
quests.explanation: "Pub" closes the lips gently after a slightly longer vowel. "Pup" clips the vowel and shuts crisply.
quests.vowelTensionRule: In final position the voiced /b/ lengthens the vowel before it, while /p/ shortens it and closes sharply.
quests.mouthPosition: Stretch the vowel slightly before /b/; cut it off sharply before /p/.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Beginning of the word. Listen for breathiness in the first sound.
quests.explanation: That was "guard": a soft start with no puff. "Card" begins with a breathy, hollow release.
quests.vowelTensionRule: The tongue back touches the soft palate for both; the audible difference is the breathy release of /k/.
quests.mouthPosition: Feel the back of the tongue press upward, and hold a tissue in front of the mouth to check the puff for /k/.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Listen to the middle sound, between the vowels.
quests.explanation: "Waver" has a buzzing /v/ in the middle. "Wafer" has a breathy /f/.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Listen for continuous voicing across the middle of the word: /v/ has it, /f/ interrupts it.
quests.mouthPosition: Feel your throat: buzzing for /v/, silence for /f/.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Middle position. Listen for a crisp tongue-tip stop or a softer, voiced one.
quests.explanation: The word was "metal": the tongue tip made a brief silent closure before the /əl/. "Medal" is voiced through the consonant.
quests.vowelTensionRule: In the middle of the word, a firm, brief closure signals /t/, and a voiced, looser closure signals /d/.
quests.mouthPosition: Touch the throat: /d/ vibrates through the closure, /t/ does not.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: The vowel is the same. Listen to the very end and to how long the vowel lasts.
quests.explanation: "Eyes" stretches the vowel and ends in a buzz. "Ice" is shorter and ends with a hiss.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Word-final /z/ often loses some voicing, but it never loses the longer vowel before it.
quests.mouthPosition: Cut the vowel short before /s/.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: At the start of the word: buzz or hiss?
quests.explanation: It was "vine": the voice buzzed while the lip touched the teeth. "Fine" begins with a breathy hiss.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /f/ and /v/ use the same lip-and-teeth position; /f/ is voiceless with strong friction, while /v/ is voiced with a softer buzz.
quests.mouthPosition: Touch the upper teeth to the lower lip. Blow air for /f/; add the voice and a buzz for /v/.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Middle of the word again, with a different pair of words. Listen to the consonant.
quests.explanation: "Lagging" has a soft, voiced /ɡ/ that flows between the vowels. "Lacking" has a crisp, silent closure.
quests.vowelTensionRule: In the middle of a word, listen for the brief silence at /k/ versus the continuous buzz through /ɡ/.
quests.mouthPosition: Touch your throat: vibration continues through /ɡ/ but stops for /k/.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Start of the word. Listen for vibration.
quests.explanation: You heard "zap": the buzz at the start was voiced. "Sap" opens with a plain hiss.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /s/ is a voiceless hiss; /z/ is the same tongue shape with the voice on, producing a buzz. Listen for a clean hiss or a buzzing sound at the beginning.
quests.mouthPosition: Place the tongue tip just behind the upper teeth with a narrow groove for air. Add voice for /z/ and keep it silent for /s/.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Final position. Focus on how the vowel and ending combine.
quests.explanation: "Peg" has a slightly longer vowel and a soft, voiced ending. "Peck" is short and finishes with a crisp stop.
quests.vowelTensionRule: At the end of a word, /ɡ/ lengthens the preceding vowel and is only lightly released; /k/ shortens it and closes with a sharper stop.
quests.mouthPosition: For /k/ shorten the vowel and close the back of the tongue at once. For /ɡ/ hold the vowel longer and close softly.
